newsitem.title: FRANCE: Congo's Lissouba says presidential poll threatened.
newsitem.headline: Congo's Lissouba says presidential poll threatened.

text.p: Congo President Pascal Lissouba said on Tuesday that a presidential election set for July 27 was threatened by continued fighting between his troops and forces loyal to former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.

"The end of July will not be possible so long as people have arms...Conditions do not permit it," Lissouba told Agence Sonor Internationale, a branch of Radio France Internationale, when asked whether the elections would still be held as scheduled.
Lissouba said he thought the election could go ahead as planned only if an international force were able to act as a buffer by physically separating the warring factions.
"Only a buffer force could help ny assuring that the people lay down their arms,"he said.
At the weekend Paris had rejected a request from Lissouba that 1,200 French soldiers then in the Congolese capital Brazzaville be left in the country to act as a buffer force.
France began withdrawing its troops on Monday after having helped evacuate more than 5,000 foreigners from the capital area.
